newsitem.title: UK: Gold Outlook - Dealers stay wary of price direction.
newsitem.headline: Gold Outlook - Dealers stay wary of price direction.

text.p: Dealers were keeping their options open on this week's trend in the gold market on Monday following last week's surge to higher levels across the whole precious metals complex.
"Gold has to get through $347-$348 to confirm that it is a buy again," one dealer said.
The metal's laggard role in the complex was shown up by the gold-silver ratio on Friday tightening to 66.58, more than 10 points down on the beginning of the year.
Platinum's premium over gold was over $20 most of last week after being under $5.00 for most of January.
"When platinum's premium over gold began to widen, it was due to weakness in gold. But the last few dollars have represented true strength in the platinum market," a dealer said.
Late last Wednesday the widely anticipated reaction to a period of depressed prices swept across the markets. What surprised dealers was the extent of the correction.
Platinum reached its highest price of the year and silver and palladium achieved their highest levels in months.
Gold lurched from a 3-3/4 year low and was up $10 at one point, before settling at no more than its best price for a week.
"Gold found something of a base between $340 and $336. It just got too expensive for the funds to force the market lower so they changed strategy and went for the upside," a market analyst said.
"It was a very clever exit strategy to lock in profits," the analyst added.

Sentiment in the gold market has been flattened by the threat and latterly reality of central banks selling gold from their reserves, confirmed by the Dutch central bank last month saying it had sold 300 tonnes of bullion from its vaults.
Additional pressure has come from gold producers borrowing gold to sell to the market in an attempt to protect their profits against ever diminishing prices.

In the background has been pressure from a surging dollar and rampant profit potential in the stock and bond markets to tempt investors interest away from a hard commodity with currently low short term profit potential like gold.

Platinum and palladium were expected to come under more pressure this week after a statement from a Moscow official on Friday that delayed talks between exports and Japanese platinum and palladium importers could start next month.

Russia, normally Japan's largest supplier of platinum group metals, has not exported this year after 1997 supply contract negotiations were postponed due to administrative and budget problems late last year.
Palladium was down sharply on Monday morning after the overbought market corrected lower in Asia and early Europe, dealers said. Platinum was also some $2.00 down from Friday's London close.
"I cannot believe there will not be a price reaction (to news that talks are to begin)," a market analyst added.

Platinum and especially palladium prices have firmed this year as consumers have covered requirements in the spot market. A further price boost came when the hedge funds saw the chance to make a quick profit in these tight, illiquid markets.
